title: The Silent Oath
premise: Astrid Oyelaran has spent three years erasing herself from every ledger in the Thornfell mountains, but a smuggled prophecy book written a century ago names her by her true name and dates her death to the winter solstice. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and guided by a disgraced archivist who believes the prophecies are forged, Astrid learns that the vanished kingdom of Vel Saren still exists behind a door only its rightful heir can open—and the prophecy insists that heir is her. To survive, she must choose between sealing herself safely inside a dead country or carrying its last magic back into a world where justice must be built, not inherited. She opens the door, refuses the crown it offers, and instead breaks the oath-magic binding Vel Saren's people to their dead kings, freeing both nations at the cost of her own recorded name.
about_author: Rosalind Eriksen is a former cartographer of disputed borders who turned to fantasy after realizing maps lie more elegantly than novels. She writes from a farmhouse in Norway, where she keeps an annotated collection of books about countries that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Astrid guides a contraband cargo through the Thornfell passes, demonstrating her mastery of smugglers' roads and her talent for being forgotten. When she pays a toll with a coin bearing Vel Saren's seal, the toll-keeper flinches as if recognizing her. POV: Astrid. Beat: uneasy competence shadowed by the first hint she is known.

chapters.title: A Date With Winter
chapters.summary: In the free city of Marrowgate, Astrid's patron shows her a century-old prophecy book: her true name, tonight's date, and the words 'the door opens on her blood.' She laughs it off—until inquisitors burn the safehouse hours later. POV: Astrid. Beat: denial cracking into fear; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Lied
chapters.summary: Fleeing Marrowgate, Astrid is cornered by Tam Vessery, a disgraced royal archivist who claims the prophecy is a forgery planted to flush out Vel Saren's hidden heir. He knows her mother's name. POV: alternating Astrid and Tam. Beat: wary alliance born of mutual blackmail and shared enemies.

chapters.title: What the Mountains Remember
chapters.summary: Traveling old Vel Saren roads that appear only at dusk, Astrid discovers the landscape itself responds to her—bridges reforming, waystones warming. Tam records each event with growing alarm. POV: Tam. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as evidence mounts that the prophecy may be genuine.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Kindness
chapters.summary: Inquisitor-General Corvane Halde offers amnesty to mountain villages in exchange for information, revealing his methodical gentleness. He interrogates the toll-keeper from chapter one. POV: Corvane. Beat: chilling antagonist established—corruption wearing the mask of order.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Astrid returns to her old mentor's ruined hedge-cottage and recovers a memory-charm her mother left: a voice describing 'the door out of a country that no longer exists.' Inquisitors arrive; the cottage burns again. POV: Astrid. Beat: grief for the childhood she ran from, resolve kindling.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Debate
chapters.summary: The free cities' council refuses to believe the usurper's armies will cross the mountains before spring. Only the smuggler-guilds vote to prepare. Astrid watches democracy fail in real time. POV: Astrid. Beat: disillusionment—the law will not save anyone.

chapters.title: Nine Names, One Grave
chapters.summary: Tam deciphers that eight heirs preceded Astrid in the prophecy; all died young, all erased from records. He confesses he helped forge documents for the usurper years ago. POV: Tam. Beat: guilt confessed, trust nearly shattered, then grudgingly rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Road Through Yesterday
chapters.summary: Pursued by Corvane's riders, Astrid leads them onto a road that loops through a single repeated day until the horses give out—a Vel Saren defense only she can navigate. POV: Astrid. Beat: her outlaw knowledge becomes literal power; first taste of agency.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane reveals he too was named in a prophecy once—as the usurper's promised instrument—and chose obedience over freedom. He offers Astrid the same bargain. POV: Corvane. Beat: mirror-antagonist; corruption shown as a choice made slowly.

chapters.title: The Door in the Water
chapters.summary: Following the memory-charm's directions, Astrid finds the door beneath a drowned lake: stone carved with her family name going back nine generations. It will not open for her yet—it wants an oath. POV: Astrid. Beat: threshold reached; the cost becomes visible.

chapters.title: An Oath Is a Chain
chapters.summary: Tam researches what the oath requires: binding one's memory to the kingdom, surrendering every personal recollection to the archive of dead kings. Astrid realizes accepting the crown means forgetting why she ever wanted freedom. POV: Tam. Beat: horror of the theme—power demands self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Burning of Marrowgate
chapters.summary: The usurper's army arrives early and sacks Marrowgate while the council dithers. Astrid saves whom she can through smuggler tunnels, including the toll-keeper's daughter. POV: Astrid. Beat: despair and fury; justice outside the law stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Verdict
chapters.summary: The guilds convene a smuggler's court—no writs, no oaths—to judge whether Astrid should be surrendered to buy peace. She argues her own case and wins by telling the whole truth, prophecy included. POV: Astrid. Beat: the book's thesis dramatized—justice kept alive by ordinary people.

chapters.title: What My Mother Chose
chapters.summary: The memory-charm plays its final layer: Astrid's mother was the ninth heir, who refused the door and paid with Astrid's recorded existence. Her invisibility was protection, not accident. POV: Astrid. Beat: rage transmuting into understanding; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Solstice March
chapters.summary: Corvane's vanguard reaches the lake on the solstice eve. The smugglers mount a delaying battle in the passes while Astrid and Tam race to the door. POV: alternating. Beat: rising action cresting; allies spending themselves for her choice.

chapters.title: The Door Opens on Her Blood
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Astrid cuts her palm and speaks the opening words—but alters them, swearing to remember rather than forget. The door opens anyway. Inside waits the archive of dead kings, offering her the crown. POV: Astrid. Beat: climax begins; defiance at the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Kingdom That Wanted to Die
chapters.summary: Within, Astrid meets the accumulated dead kings, who reveal Vel Saren bound itself to oath-magic to escape a greater conquest long ago—and has been dying of it since. They beg her to end it. POV: Astrid. Beat: revelation reframing everything; compassion for the enemy within.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Astrid shatters the oath-magic instead of inheriting it, unbinding Vel Saren's people and dissolving the kingdom into the living world. The backlash erases her own name from every record—including the prophecy. POV: Astrid. Beat: climax resolved through refusal; power renounced at its peak.

chapters.title: Corvane Unbound
chapters.summary: With the prophecy broken, Corvane's ordained role collapses; the usurper discards him as an instrument that failed. Astrid spares him, leaving him to live without destiny's excuse. POV: Corvane. Beat: antagonist's fall; corruption exposed as hollow when the script ends.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own Making
chapters.summary: Spring comes. Astrid, now simply 'Ash,' helps rebuild Marrowgate alongside freed Vel Saren refugees, teaching smuggler roads to those with nowhere else to go. Tam begins writing an honest history. POV: Tam. Beat: quiet resolution; community replacing kingdom.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Page
chapters.summary: Astrid finds the prophecy book's final page blank where her death-date used to be. She leaves it that way, walks an open road under her own chosen name, and does not look back. POV: Astrid. Beat: thematic closure—memory kept, future unwritten, freedom chosen.
